V1.adjudication_rule: lead_type: a lead is coined_name when it is, or is headed by, a proper-noun-like label: an invented or blended word or acronym, a dictionary word used as the name of one specific artefact (including existing techniques), a phrase followed by its parenthesised acronym or its own symbol, or a non-literal noun phrase that the subtitle presents as the paper's artefact. A lead made of ordinary words in their ordinary or standard technical senses is descriptive_phrase even when it is the paper's method name ('method description' in codebook A, 'approach in ordinary language' in codebook B), as is a lead in which a pre-existing name or family abbreviation only modifies a generic head (codebook A: 'LoRA Fine-Tuning at Scale'). Metaphors, puns and allusions that the subtitle does not present as an artefact are slogans (descriptive_phrase). This matches 239 of the 255 agreed plain multi-word leads (both passes descriptive). orthography: the codebook's ordered rules applied to the name (an initial article is not part of the name). casing: tokens the authors treat as names (coined names, acronym expansions, established architecture names) are set aside; field and family terms are counted.
